newsitem.title: USA: Republican chief blasts "liberal media" coverage.
newsitem.headline: Republican chief blasts "liberal media" coverage.

text.p: Republican Party Chairman Haley Barbour said Wednesday Bob Dole has a "genuine real chance" to win the presidency despite efforts by the "liberal media elite" to write off his chances of victory.

Barbour said in a telephone conference call with reporters that, despite the unfavourable press and television coverage he sees and the fact that the Republican is far behind in polls, Dole can catch President Clinton in just 13 days.

Predicting that no one will get 50 percent of the vote on Nov. 5, Barbour said, "The winner will get 47 or 48 percent. And I think the difference between the winner and loser will be very small and that Dole absolutely has a genuine real chance to be the winner."
He added, "I think Dole can win. I think he has a real chance to win ... people don't like being told by the media that the election is over."

In his daily scheduled conference telephone call with reporters from several news organisations, Barbour took on the media Wednesday. "From the beginning we've recognised that we shouldn't rely on the liberal media elite to trumpet our message for us. So that's why we tried to create other outlets to communicate directly with the voters so that our message is not filtered through anybody," he said.

Barbour gave a thumbs down review of coverage of the campaign this year and pointed to a Washington Post headline Sunday that he said, with exaggeration, was "three inches tall" predicting a Clinton landslide victory.

"There have been news organisations that have been wanting to say this election was over for months," he said. "There has been less coverage of this presidential campaign, particularly by the television network news, than has been the case in the past. The coverage that there has been has been much more fixated on the process, the horserace, inside baseball, rather than the issues that affect voters families, communities and the country. People don't much like that."
But Barbour said he did not think the media was joining together in opposition.

"I don't think there's some conspiracy here that all the press meets every day at 10 o'clock and says how are we going to screw the Republicans today, but the fact is there's less coverage," he said, adding, "The media elite tend to look at issues from a different perspective than most voters."

He lashed out at the New York Times, which he called the "best friend that the Democrats have," for a front-page story Wednesday with the headline "GOP pushes Congress strategy that shuns Dole." The story said Republican campaign operatives are urging congressional candidates to cut loose from Dole.
He repeated what he told reporters Tuesday, that the first goal of the party is to elect Dole with a Republican Congress.
